newsitem.title: USA: "Relic" beats "Evita" to top U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Relic" beats "Evita" to top U.S. box office.

text.p: The big screen version of "Evita" was left crying over the weekend as an unheralded horror movie beat it to the number one spot at the box office, according to studio estimates released Sunday.
"The Relic," a serial murder thriller starring Tom Sizemore and Penelope Ann Miller, took in $9.4 million in ticket sales the weekend it opened.

"Evita," the highly publicized musical starring Madonna and Antonio Banderas, earned $8.6 million in its first weekend of release. Walt Disney Co. released the movie in a handful of theaters on Christmas Day. The movie, produced by Cinergi Pictures Entertainment Inc., features songs such as "Don't Cry for Me Argentina."
In third place was John Travolta's angel movie "Michael" with $8.5 million in sales at the box office. It had held the number one spot the past two weeks.

"Evita," however, was playing on one-third the screens of "The Relic" -- 704 vs. 2,095 -- and averaged a hefty $12,216 per screen vs. a modest $4,496 for "The Relic." "Evita" was 20th last weekend on 22 screens and has earned $11.5 million to date. "The Relic" is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc..

"The People Vs. Larry Flynt," which topped the year-end lists of many critics, took in $5.6 million to rank seventh, up from 22nd last weekend. The movie, which stars Woody Harrelson as the pugnacious purveyor of porn, averaged $4,542 per screen. Its three-week total is $7.7 million.
"We were probably hoping to do closer to six (million dollars)," said a spokesman for Sony Corp. unit Columbia Pictures, which released the picture.
Third-placed "Michael," released by Time Warner Inc.'s New Line Cinema, has earned $62 million since opening on Christmas Day.
Slipping two places to fourth was the hit Tom Cruise romantic comedy "Jerry Maguire," with $7.8 million in sales. The Sony release has taken in $94.1 million so far.

Also down two places was "Scream," a horror movie described as a cross between "Psycho" and "Clueless." The movie, the surprise hit of the holiday season, took in $7.6 million for a total $50.1 million to date. The film is released by Disney-owned Miramax Films.

The other new entries in the top 10 were "Jackie Chan's First Strike," in sixth place with $6.5 million in ticket sales and "Turbulence," an airplane disaster movie starring Ray Liotta, eighth with $4.4 million in receipts.
The ticket sales are based on studio estimates collected by Exhibitor Relations Co. Inc.
